1.1.1.path: Cask Guild › Wine Academy › Testable Red
1.1.1.definition: Testable Red is a group of 14 entries in the Wine Academy. It includes Cabernet Sauvignon, Merlot, Pinot Noir….

1.1.1.1.path: Cask Guild › Wine Academy › Testable Red › Cabernet Sauvignon
1.1.1.1.definition: Red wine grape of Bordeaux origin, a natural cross of Cabernet Franc and Sauvignon Blanc; thick-skinned and tannic, widely planted worldwide.

1.1.1.2.path: Cask Guild › Wine Academy › Testable Red › Merlot
1.1.1.2.definition: Red wine grape from Bordeaux, softer and earlier-ripening than Cabernet Sauvignon; a major blending partner on Bordeaux's Right Bank.

1.1.1.3.path: Cask Guild › Wine Academy › Testable Red › Pinot Noir
1.1.1.3.definition: Thin-skinned red grape of Burgundy, also a core Champagne grape; known for light-to-medium body and sensitivity to site.

1.1.1.4.path: Cask Guild › Wine Academy › Testable Red › Syrah/Shiraz
1.1.1.4.definition: Red grape from the northern Rhône (Syrah), called Shiraz in Australia; deeply colored with peppery, dark-fruit character.

1.1.1.5.path: Cask Guild › Wine Academy › Testable Red › Grenache/Garnacha
1.1.1.5.definition: Warm-climate red grape (Garnacha in Spain), central to Southern Rhône blends and Priorat.

1.1.1.6.path: Cask Guild › Wine Academy › Testable Red › Tempranillo
1.1.1.6.definition: Spain's leading red grape, the backbone of Rioja and Ribera del Duero (where it is called Tinto Fino).

1.1.1.7.path: Cask Guild › Wine Academy › Testable Red › Sangiovese
1.1.1.7.definition: Italy's most planted red grape and the base of Chianti, Brunello di Montalcino and Vino Nobile.

1.1.1.8.path: Cask Guild › Wine Academy › Testable Red › Nebbiolo
1.1.1.8.definition: Late-ripening, high-tannin, high-acid red grape of Piedmont, used for Barolo and Barbaresco.

1.1.1.9.path: Cask Guild › Wine Academy › Testable Red › Malbec
1.1.1.9.definition: Red grape originally from southwest France (Cahors), now best known from Argentina.

1.1.1.10.path: Cask Guild › Wine Academy › Testable Red › Zinfandel/Primitivo
1.1.1.10.definition: Red grape genetically identical to Croatian Tribidrag; known as Zinfandel in California and Primitivo in Puglia.

1.1.1.11.path: Cask Guild › Wine Academy › Testable Red › Cabernet Franc
1.1.1.11.definition: Red grape from Bordeaux and the Loire; a parent of Cabernet Sauvignon and Merlot.

1.1.1.12.path: Cask Guild › Wine Academy › Testable Red › Gamay
1.1.1.12.definition: Red grape of Beaujolais, making light, fruity reds.

1.1.1.13.path: Cask Guild › Wine Academy › Testable Red › Barbera
1.1.1.13.definition: Barbera. Listed under Testable Red in the Wine Academy. A fuller definition has not been written yet.

1.1.1.14.path: Cask Guild › Wine Academy › Testable Red › Mourvèdre/Monastrell
1.1.1.14.definition: Late-ripening red grape of Spain (Monastrell) and southern France (Mourvèdre, e.g. Bandol).

1.1.2.path: Cask Guild › Wine Academy › Testable White
1.1.2.definition: Testable White is a group of 12 entries in the Wine Academy. It includes Chardonnay, Sauvignon Blanc, Riesling….

1.1.2.1.path: Cask Guild › Wine Academy › Testable White › Chardonnay
1.1.2.1.definition: White grape of Burgundy and Champagne; flexible in style from lean and unoaked to rich and barrel-fermented.

1.1.2.2.path: Cask Guild › Wine Academy › Testable White › Sauvignon Blanc
1.1.2.2.definition: Aromatic white grape from the Loire and Bordeaux, typically high in acidity with herbaceous or citrus aromas.

1.1.2.3.path: Cask Guild › Wine Academy › Testable White › Riesling
1.1.2.3.definition: Aromatic white grape most associated with Germany and Alsace; high acidity, made from bone-dry to very sweet.

1.1.2.4.path: Cask Guild › Wine Academy › Testable White › Pinot Grigio/Gris
1.1.2.4.definition: Grey-pink-skinned mutation of Pinot Noir; called Pinot Grigio in Italy and Pinot Gris in France.

1.1.2.5.path: Cask Guild › Wine Academy › Testable White › Chenin Blanc
1.1.2.5.definition: High-acid white grape of the Loire Valley, made dry, sweet and sparkling; also important in South Africa.

1.1.2.6.path: Cask Guild › Wine Academy › Testable White › Gewürztraminer
1.1.2.6.definition: Very aromatic, pink-skinned white grape (an aromatic form of Savagnin), notable in Alsace.

1.1.2.7.path: Cask Guild › Wine Academy › Testable White › Viognier
1.1.2.7.definition: Aromatic white grape of the northern Rhône (Condrieu).

1.1.2.8.path: Cask Guild › Wine Academy › Testable White › Albariño
1.1.2.8.definition: Aromatic, high-acid white grape of Rías Baixas (Spain), called Alvarinho in Portugal.

1.1.2.9.path: Cask Guild › Wine Academy › Testable White › Grüner Veltliner
1.1.2.9.definition: Austria's signature white grape, often with peppery notes.

1.1.2.10.path: Cask Guild › Wine Academy › Testable White › Sémillon
1.1.2.10.definition: White grape of Bordeaux, the main grape of Sauternes and prone to noble rot.

Austrian PDO: Sekt Austria / Reserve / Große Reserve per Sektbezeichnungsverordnung (Klassik no longer permitted for new labels); Reserve & Große Reserve = traditional method only. 1.3.28.path: Cask Guild › Spirits Academy › Aging Requirements › Tequila (NOM-006)
1.3.28.definition: Tequila (NOM-006) is a group of 5 entries in the Spirits Academy, under Aging Requirements. It includes Blanco/Plata · no aging (may rest <2 mo), Joven/Oro · blend or abocado, Reposado · 2+ mo oak….
facts: Blanco/Plata: no abocante, may mature <2 months in oak/encino (§4.36.1). Joven/Oro: blanco blended with reposado/añejo/extra añejo, or blanco mellowed with permitted abocado ingredients (§4.36.2). Aged classes: oak or holm-oak (encino), direct contact. Reposado has NO vessel-size limit and no legal upper bound (the popular '2–12 months' reflects that ≥1 yr in ≤600 L qualifies as Añejo). Source: NOM-006-SCFI-2012 §4.36 (DOF 13-12-2012) [verified online 2026-10-12]
